correctness.rationale: Exact local best-response inequalities reduce nonuniform equilibria to |X|,|Y|<=1. Even n forces X=Y=0 and equality on each deleted pair, yielding a binomial convolution. Odd n has X,Y=±1; equal-sign solutions require (n+1)/2 deleted pairs of the majority sign, and cross-sign solutions require exactly one unmatched or one unequal deleted pair, forcing t=n-1 or n. The crossing-edge identity (n²-XY)/2 minus unequal deleted pairs proves all exact welfare and parity-threshold claims including n=t=2. An independent exhaustive adjacency-payoff check tested all 757296 configurations on 42 instances with 2<=n<=8, every 0<=t<=n, and verified equilibrium counts and welfare histograms; the all-n proof is algebraic, not extrapolated from enumeration.

value.rationale: Matching deletion is the canonical controlled perturbation of a dense two-community anti-coordination graph. Exact equilibrium-count and cut histogram formulas and a sharp odd-size onset of inefficiency after only (n+1)/2 deleted edges identify a structural stability boundary. They quantify edge-failure sensitivity and high-welfare local stability beyond generic half-optimal Nash bounds, without requiring a paper-sized general theory. This is a natural full-parameter family, not a single arbitrary numerical slice or textbook restatement.
